Did not treat missing GA4 as zero. Ended baseline-collection status and opened a three-post relevance-led LinkedIn hook experiment while preserving schedule, UTM and editorial guardrails.

Confirmed production and both reporting endpoints healthy; analyzed 7-day and 28-day acquisition, engagement, content, conversion and LinkedIn data; incorporated the full available publishing history; identified unavailable 90-day, prior-period and year-over-year comparisons without blocking action; set dated numerical goals; and assigned concrete work to publishing, distribution, growth, conversion, analytics and reliability roles.

entries.trigger: Scheduled reliability check found the production Buffer metrics feed falsely labeling repository-UTM-tagged CUAI LinkedIn posts as untracked because it required the exact distribution URL to appear in Buffer's returned post text.
entries.summary: Confirmed the August 12 publisher cycle, live article, homepage and production runtime were healthy. Recovered a material Buffer reporting false negative by reconciling approved repository distribution URLs as UTM evidence when Buffer does not echo the exact sent URL. Validated the narrow fix on a READY preview, merged PR #119, verified the resulting production deployment READY, and confirmed the live Buffer endpoint now reports tracked recent posts correctly while preserving the pre-tracking EricaAssist exception. No sent post, credential, schedule, destination, editorial gate or social limit changed.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 12 publisher cycle and morning reliability recovery.
entries.summary: Confirmed production, GA4 and Buffer healthy after the morning UTM reconciliation recovery; reviewed the August 12 Library Insight and current coverage state; found 7-day users, sessions and views running ahead of the 28-day weekly pace while engaged sessions and engagement rate lag; identified LinkedIn reach and qualified onsite engagement as the distribution constraint; kept the relevance-led experiment active without forcing a High story; and assigned concrete growth, conversion, distribution, analytics and reliability work. Search Console remains isolated as an optional incompatible Data API query, and stale draft PR #118 must not be merged wholesale because its UTM work is superseded by PR #119.

entries.summary: Diagnosed a stale LinkedIn handoff after the authoritative policy changed later in the day. The article itself and production were healthy. Because Wednesday's fixed 11:30 a.m. ET slot had passed, reserved the next eligible fixed slot—Thursday August 13 at 11:30 a.m. ET—using the approved company-page workflow, exact CUAI UTMs and existing hero image. Validated a READY preview, merged PR #123, verified production READY on the exact deployed commit, invoked the tracked scheduler once, and received HTTP 201/ok=true with Buffer post 6a7ce17164b274b4d967ad74 scheduled for 2026-08-13T15:30:00Z. No duplicate, credential, destination, editorial gate, or cadence limit changed. Prevention recommendation: any future eligibility-policy change affecting a same-day publication should explicitly reconcile that publication against the social queue before the policy PR is considered operationally complete.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 13 publisher cycle and the August 12 Library-Insight LinkedIn policy recovery.

Joined current Buffer and GA4 funnel: 24 impressions and 16 reach across two current metrics-ready posts produced 3 attributable LinkedIn sessions and 1 engaged session. Found user volume holding above the 28-day weekly pace but page-view and engaged-session pace materially weaker, making onsite depth the primary growth constraint. Search Console remains degraded by the same incompatible GA4 dimension/metric request; root cause is established in stale PR #118, but a fresh repair branch attempt was blocked by the GitHub write safety layer, so no reporting code changed in this run. Updated the CEO report and usage ledger on a dedicated reporting branch.

entries.trigger: Scheduled reliability check followed up the repeated Search Console reporting incompatibility already identified by the CEO while verifying the August 13 publisher, social handoff and production runtime.
entries.summary: Confirmed the August 13 publisher cycle, current social reservations, Buffer handoff and Vercel runtime were healthy; the recovered vendor-exit LinkedIn item sent at the fixed 11:30 a.m. ET slot with approved UTMs and no duplicate. Investigated the repeated optional Search Console failure in the GA4 reporting feed. Two narrow repairs (#126 and #127) each passed READY preview/build validation but failed the Production-only Google Analytics Data API check: the first used an invalid dimension and the second still returned an incompatible dimensions/metrics error. Immediately rolled both speculative changes back in PR #128, restored the pre-repair reporting code, verified Production READY on commit 20f4d45, and confirmed core GA4 remains HTTP 200. Search Console reporting remains isolated and degraded; the next safe path is a documented direct Search Console reporting/API integration rather than another speculative GA4 Core Reporting query. No credentials, tracking, editorial rules, social destination, cadence limits or publishing behavior changed.

Reviewed the isolated direct Search Console API probe; its preview is READY but returns search_console_service_account_missing, so it remains unmerged under the fully-validated-change rule. Updated the CEO report and usage ledger with dated goals and owner commitments.

entries.trigger: Weekday CUAI CEO operating review after the August 21 publisher cycle, with mandatory live GA4/Buffer/Search Console retrieval and active optimization.

Current seven-day engagement rate recovered to 34.5% versus 36.4% over 28 days, but active users, sessions, page views, engaged sessions and 90% scrolling remain materially below the 28-day weekly pace; acquisition detail shows the contraction is concentrated in direct traffic while Google organic sessions are above their 28-day weekly pace. The NCUA article completes the three-article decision-first cohort; closed that experiment with a revise decision because the engagement-rate target is met but absolute depth/user guardrails are not, retaining early decision clarity as editorial discretion rather than a forced template. Identified a mission-fit gap because today's otherwise useful article is general governance rather than substantive AI/technology intelligence, so strengthened the publisher policy and publishing rules prospectively to require a source-supported AI/technology operating implication while grandfathering today's already-published and scheduled package. Today's 12:30 p.m. ET NCUA LinkedIn post is the first scheduled operating-tension experiment observation. Refreshed the CEO report and workload ledger on a READY Preview branch.

entries.trigger: Reliability review found automation/publishing-rules.json still defined article-cycle completion as one full article plus three Alerts even though the authoritative daily article task and newsroom runbook assign Alerts to a separate single-purpose cycle.
entries.summary: Diagnosed an internal workflow-contract drift, not a publisher, Alert-service, Buffer or production outage. The authoritative Publish CUAI Daily Article policy explicitly owns one article plus bounded LinkedIn distribution and does not authorize Alerts, while the newsroom runbook separates Article and Alert cycles; stale publishing-rules completion wording still required one article and three Alerts in the same standard cycle. Clarified cycle ownership so the article cycle completes after one valid article (or exhaustion of qualified article candidates) and the separate Alert cycle retains the three-alert daily target. Today’s article outcome is complete and live, Production is READY with no runtime errors, Buffer is HTTP 200/ok=true, and the unique Friday 12:30 p.m. ET company-page reservation remains not yet due with immutable UTMs. No Alert, social post, credential, schedule, destination, editorial/source gate or published content was created or changed. Durable prevention: keep completion semantics scoped to the cycle that owns the work whenever newsroom responsibilities are split.
